page: Microsoft Azure E20a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 10 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 160.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 512 GB, and there are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the poor category, representing the bottom 10% of tested systems. However, multi-core performance under stress-ng and Geekbench scales to average levels. Memory performance is a notable strength, with the PassMark memory score ranking as strong, placing in the top 25%. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 78.56 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is measured at 44.51 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is configured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-core compute performance. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications such as database operations, caching layers, and text processing, where the PassMark database operations and Redis SET benchmarks demonstrate average performance. Conversely, tasks like medium-model LLM text generation show weak performance, making this server less suitable for complex AI inference workloads.
